summary: Tucked into a narrow, redwood-shaded canyon between the southern flanks of Mount Tamalpais and the tidal flats of Richardson Bay, this census-designated place of roughly 12,000 people occupies just 4.7 square miles yet sits within immediate striking distance of some of the most celebrated trail networks in the Bay Area — the Dipsea Trail to Stinson Beach, Muir Woods, and the ridgeline fire roads above Mill Valley all start practically at the neighborhood's edge. That access comes at a price: a median home value north of $1.8 million against a median household income of about $238,000 translates to a price-to-income ratio above 7.6, meaning even at the local median income, purchasing requires substantial savings or equity beyond current earnings. The area functions almost entirely as a bedroom community; there is no significant commercial district or employer base, and most working residents commute south toward San Francisco — roughly a 30-minute drive or a combination of feeder bus to the Sausalito ferry — which means daily life revolves around the car despite the compact footprint. Daytime highs averaging just 64°F year-round, with coastal fog suppressing summer heat, create a climate that feels more like perpetual late spring than stereotypical California. The defining tension is geographic: extraordinary natural beauty and trail access paired with canyon-carved roads that make even a grocery run feel like a winding expedition.
